sentences.text:
THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR PRELIMINARY HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 ORDER

The petitioner has sought for consideration of the petitioner's representation dated 18.04.2023 for grant of compensation for the land bearing Survey No.643, Kasaba Hobli, Gramathana measuring 40 sq.ft x 12 sq.ft [totally 480 Sq.ft.].
2.

In terms of the detailed report at Annexures - A, B and C, the petitioner has sought for fixation of compensation amount as per the judgment and award in LAC.No.28/2019 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Hassan dated 7.10.2014.
3.

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The petitioner submits that he is the owner of land bearing Survey No.643 which is situated adjacent to NC: 2023:KHC:21148 Bangalore-Mangalore road and at the time of widening the Bangalore-Mangalore Highway road, the road was widened without following due process of law and no compensation was paid for his land to an extent of 480 sq.ft..
The petitioner further submits that while quantifying the compensation, the Court ought to have taken note of the guidelines including the details mentioned in Paragraph-3 of the petitions.

The petitioner further submits that insofar as the adjacent land owners whose lands have been utilised for road widening, the proceedings have culminated in LAC No.28/2010 and compensation has been enhanced to Rs.7,000/- per square foot along with statutory benefits.
It is submitted that as the petitioner is placed on parity with the claimant in LAC No.28/2010, he is entitled to the same compensation.

4. The Counsel for the petitioner points out that in terms of the proceedings at Annexure-G, a list has been prepared of private land owners whose lands were initially sought to be notified for acquisition but subsequently left NC: 2023:KHC:21148 out and that the land of land owners mentioned at Annexure-G have been utilised and writ petitions filed by some of such land owners,
whose names are mentioned at Sl.Nos.1 and 3, viz., H.V.Ramanaraju, son of H.S.Venkatesha Murthy and H.S.Venkatesha Murthy, son of Subbaraya Shetty have been disposed off in W.P.No.50178/2019 connected with W.P. No.181/2020 on 22.02.2021 passing certain directions.
Accordingly, it is submitted that the present petition may be disposed off on same terms while also taking note of the compensation fixed in LAC No.28/2010.
It is submitted that if petitioner stands on parity as the land-loser who has obtained enhancement in LAC No.28/2010 the same may be followed in the case of the petitioner also.
5. Heard both sides.
Perused the order in W.P.No.50178/2019 connected with W.P. No.181/2020.

The observations at Paragraphs - 5 to 10 are extracted hereinbelow for reference:
NC: 2023:KHC:21148 "5.

Though learned Additional Government Advocate submits that proceedings are conducted on 09.08.2018 in which owners had participated and price was fixed, said aspect is disputed by the learned counsel for the petitioners.

It is H.S.Yathiraj vs The Deputy Secretary on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157715757/
3 also to be noticed that there are no records as regards consensual price fixation that is coming forth from the respondents' side.

sentences.text:
It is noticed that in the proceedings of the Deputy Commissioner though there is a reference to price fixation at Rs.3,000/-
per sq. ft. with respect to the properties in Hassan Town made use of for the purpose of widening of the road, learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the said price fixation is not accepted.
6.

Taking note that though the petitioners have given letter of consent, consent to be construed as being limited for the purpose of utilisation of the properties of the petitioners for the purpose of road widening and as regards the question of price fixation, in light of the absence of consent,
matter requires adjudication as per law.

7. Learned counsel appearing for the respondent - State submits that as per the proceedings at Annexure-R1 the Deputy Commissioner has fixed the price at Rs.3,000/- per sq. ft. which the petitioners ought to have NC: 2023:KHC:21148 accepted.

However, in light of the absence of consent as regards price fixation, petitioners' right to seek for compensation as per the legal entitlement in accordance with the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 (for short 'the Act') is kept open.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 8. It is noticed that the respondent - Authority has stated that as the petitioners have not come forward to accept the offer as regards compensation made by the respondents, necessary proceedings would be made for passing of award and disbursing the compensation in terms of the Act.

In light of the admitted position that the petitioners' lands have been made use of without acquisition and as the offer of acquiring the petitioners' properties by outright purchase has not been fructified due to the absence of agreement as regards to price, the respondents to complete the acquisition process in terms of the provisions of the Act and disburse the compensation.

9. Insofar as the petitioners' right for claim of compensation beyond the amount of Rs.3,000/- or as may be fixed afresh by the respondent authority, petitioners are reserved liberty to pursue the remedy as per the Act by seeking for appropriate reference in terms of Section 64 of the Act in NC:
2023:KHC:21148 accordance with law.

It is also made clear that in light of the petitioners' properties not having been notified though utilised, in the absence of any consensus for outright purchase by the petitioners, the only remedy to the respondent - Authority is to initiate and complete acquisition process and pass award and disburse compensation.
The whole of such procedure to be completed within a period not later than twelve weeks from the date of release of this order.
10. The acquisition process to be made by the 2nd respondent while keeping it open for the 2nd respondent to make necessary payment.

However, it is made clear that in light of petitioners'
properties having been utilised way back in the year 2005 as indicated, the time limit of twelve weeks for completion of process of acquisition and disbursal of admitted compensation to be concluded without any lapse."
H.S.Yathiraj vs The Deputy Secretary on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/157715757/
4 6.
The petition is disposed off taking note of the observations extracted hereinabove and on same terms.

The contentions of the respondents are kept open and if the respondents arrive at a finding that the petitioner is similarly placed as that of the claimant - land loser, who is NC:
2023:KHC:21148 the petitioner in W.P.No.50178/2019, the petitioner is entitled for the same treatment.
Insofar as the price fixation is concerned, it is needless to state that the respondent -authorities may take note of the order passed in LAC No.28/2010.

In terms of the directions issued in W.P.No.50178/2019 connected with W.P. No.181/2020, the time limit prescribed for completion of process of acquisition and disbursement of compensation to be concluded within a time limit of 12 weeks as observed in Para-10 of the aforesaid writ petitions.
All contentions are left open.
